summary: Routing indexer cache invalidation gap after SLA-template migration causing stale route attachments
description: Issue summary: After the templating service migration carried out on 2026-03-09, several customer routes continued to inherit old SLA attachments for up to 36 hours. Impact: Incorrect SLA mapping caused mis-prioritization of internal queues and at least one delayed escalation (observed for internal routing only). This ticket tracks root cause, mitigation, and permanent fix for cache invalidation behavior in the routing indexer during template migrations.
impact: Internal routing buckets had stale SLA weights for ~1–36 hours in us-east. No customer-facing downtime observed, but internal SLAs and alerting were mis-triggered (support queue imbalance). Potential for misrouted P1s if not fixed before next migration.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) On staging, deploy templating-service version v3.12 with migration flag ON. 2) Trigger template re-authoring job (confluence runbook step 4). 3) Observe routing-indexer logs for 'template-change' events and cache refresh messages. 4) Query /routing/api/v1/effective-sla?route=<route-id> immediately after migration and again 10–20 minutes later. Expected: effective SLA reflects latest template within 60s; Observed: some routes still return previous SLA until indexer restart.
investigation_notes: - Timeline: migration executed 2026-03-09 02:14 UTC per runbook. Alerts about queue imbalance started 2026-03-09 03:05 UTC. First triage performed by on-call at 03:20 UTC. - Hypothesis A: indexer listens to templating-change events but dedup logic suppressed refresh when event payload changed ID format. - Hypothesis B: cache manager uses last-modified timestamp derived from template metadata; migration rewrote templates with preserved timestamp field causing no-op refresh. - Evidence: indexer logs show 'skip-refresh: no-timestamp-delta' for ~320 routes. See logs snippet in 'logs' field. - Relevant config: indexer batch window = 2m, cache-ttl = 24h, event-dedup = 5m. These settings explain why stale entries persisted beyond expected window during large migration.

temporary_mitigation: 1) Restarted routing-indexer workers in us-east at 2026-03-09 04:02 UTC to force cache reload (reduced window for stale entries). 2) Manually re-applied SLA attachments for 14 high-priority routes via admin tool (admin-audit#847). 3) Added temporary alert to detect 'skip-refresh' log rate > 50 in 1h window.
proposed_fix: A. Update indexer to treat migration events with preserved timestamps as 'schema-change' and force refresh regardless of timestamp delta. B. Add a migration-mode flag that bypasses event-dedup during templating-service migrations. C. Reduce cache-ttl for SLA attachments to 1h and add configurable short-circuit for template-change events. D. Add unit/integration tests simulating preserved-timestamp migrations.
work_items: patch: routing-indexer: treat preserved-timestamp events as force-refresh
config: add migration-mode flag to templating-service event publisher
infra: lower SLA attachment cache-ttl to 3600s for 48h post-deployment
tests: add migration simulation to CI
comments: Nora Patel (Support) 2026-03-09: Customer queues mis-prioritized, internal escalation delayed. Escalated to Platform SRE.
Aida Gomez (SRE) 2026-03-09: Performed indexer restart; initial manual fixes applied to critical routes. Will collect logs for full root cause.
Evan Chen (Templating) 2026-03-10: Migration tool intentionally preserved 'last_modified' to maintain external audit timestamps. We didn't anticipate indexer relying on that field to detect changes.
Liam O'Connor (Assignee) 2026-03-11: Drafting change to indexer event handling. PR reference added (github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821). Planning staged rollout to prod with kill-switch.
Megan Li (Support Ops) 2026-03-12: Added temporary watch dashboard on Grafana panel 'routing.skip_refresh_rate' and notified on-call via #support-alerts channel.
resolution: In progress: hotfix PR created and under review. Temporary mitigations applied reduced customer-facing risk. Permanent change scheduled for 2026-03-18 maintenance window. Post-deployment, we'll run targeted queries to confirm no stale SLA attachments remain and file a short postmortem.
root_cause: Indexer cache invalidation relied on a 'last_modified' delta check that failed when the templating migration intentionally preserved timestamps. Event dedup logic suppressed necessary refreshes during a bulk migration.
postmortem_followups: - Update runbook to include indexer forced-refresh step after large template migrations. - Add integration test covering preserved-timestamp migrations. - Monitor same-day migrations for next 30 days and report weekly to #platform-ops.
notes: Ticket created from Platform SRE triage during migration. Low customer exposure but high operational risk if repeated.
